dse_runs.notes: System spec: bursty Poisson arrivals (bursts of 8, 2 req/us avg), p99 latency <= 0.4us is only screened by an analytic bound at L1, so favour designs with real throughput/latency headroom (pipelined / higher n_iter throughput) that survive L2. Constraint throughput_msps >= 2 is easy; error <= 2^-10 needs enough iterations. Select rule is min luts_plus_ffs, so keep small-area designs alive, plus points spanning accuracy for a well-mapped front.

final_text: The queue held one spec, `bursty_offload`, and it is now finalized. I spent its entire L1 budget (400/400 evals) in a single structured `run_dse`, which converged to a 33-design feasible, non-dominated front spanning accuracy 10.9–12.9 bits at 903–1157 LUT+FF — notably all pipelined_m designs; the min-area end of that front dominated. Because this is a system spec whose `sys_*` numbers are only analytic bounds until simulated, I ran `simulate_system` on the front's top 5: the analytic p99 bounds (0.143–0.199 us) were indeed optimistic, with simulated p99 landing at 0.208–0.283 us, yet all five stayed under the 0.4 us requirement and the winner was unchanged — so no re-selection was needed. The ladder rungs L3–L5 (`verify_rtl`, `synthesize`, `back_annotate`) returned no recorded data for the selected design (`no_measured_data`, W=19 exhaustive RTL too heavy for a live run), so no winner change was flagged and `reexplore` was correctly skipped; the final selection therefore rests on L1 estimates plus L2 simulation only. The finalized pick is `pipelined_m: data_width=19, n_iter=12, angle_guard=0, frac_guard=0, rounding=trunc, m=7` — luts_plus_ffs=903 (736 LUTs + 167 FFs, estimated), accuracy_bits=10.9 (max_abs_err=0.000525 ≤ 2^-10), throughput 56.8 Msps ≥ 2, and simulated sys_p99_latency_us=0.245 ≤ 0.4, selected by the spec's min-luts_plus_ffs rule. Lessons worth keeping: for bursty-latency specs the L1 analytic p99 bound understates simulated latency by ~40%, so leave real headroom, and note that area-optimal points here were not the most accurate ones — the front trade-off is genuinely live.
